title: The structure sheaf of rings on the small pro-etale site
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ its small pro-etale site
[def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site]. The *structure sheaf* $\mathcal O_S$ on
$S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is the presheaf of commutative rings

$$
 \mathcal O_S(U)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)\qquad(U\to S\text{ weakly etale}),
$$

whose restriction map along a morphism $h:V\to U$ over $S$ is the ring map
$h^\sharp:\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ on global sections. Here $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)=\mathcal O_U(U)$ is the ring of sections over the whole scheme $U$, and $h^\sharp$ is the component over $U$ of the morphism of structure sheaves of $h$. It is a
sheaf of rings on $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$: as a presheaf of sets it is isomorphic to
$U\mapsto\operatorname{Mor}(U,\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[t])$ (a morphism to
$\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[t]$ is a ring map $\mathbf Z[t]\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$,
i.e. a global section), where $\operatorname{Spec}$ is the spectrum construction [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; hence it is representable on schemes and satisfies the sheaf
condition for fpqc coverings; the coverings of $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are fpqc coverings,
and the sheaf condition for a presheaf of rings is that of its underlying presheaf of
sets.

proof.text: Use the objects and morphisms of [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site]. For each scheme $U$ [def-pc-scheme] take the ring $\mathcal O_U(U)$; for a morphism $h:V\to U$, take the component $\mathcal O_U(U)\to\mathcal O_V(h^{-1}U)=\mathcal O_V(V)$ of its morphism of structure sheaves. It is a ring homomorphism by the definition of a scheme morphism. The identity morphism gives the identity component, and for $k:W\to V$ the component for $h\circ k$ is $k^\sharp\circ h^\sharp$ by the definition of composition of ringed-space morphisms. Thus these values and restrictions form the required presheaf of commutative rings.

source.place: Definitions 03P4 (definition-additive-sheaf), part (1), and 04HS (definition-structure-sheaf); definition of scheme morphism; small-site objects from 098K (proetale.tex, definition-big-small-proetale)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] to the arbitrary scheme $U$ and the commutative ring $\mathbf Z[t]$. It gives a bijection between morphisms $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[t]$ and ring maps $\mathbf Z[t]\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Evaluation at $t$ identifies the latter with $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$: the inverse sends $s$ to the map $\sum a_jt^j\mapsto\sum a_js^j$. For $h:V\to U$ the element corresponding to $a\circ h$ is $h^\sharp(a^\sharp(t))$, because pullback of global sections respects composition. Thus the bijections commute with every restriction map. This proves representability on the category of all schemes and the claimed natural identification on the small site; it does not assert that the representing affine line is itself a weakly etale object over $S$.

source.place: Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine); polynomial evaluation, applied to the presheaf of 03P4 (1)

proof.text: Let $\{f_i:U_i\to U\}$ be a covering family of the small site, and let $s_i\in\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_{U_i})$ be a matching family. Its overlaps $U_i\times_U U_j$ are objects of the small site: the projection to $U_i$ is the base change of the weakly etale map $f_j$ and is weakly etale; its composite to $S$ is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. The maps $f_j$ are weakly etale by the morphism clause of [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site]. Step 2 turns the $s_i$ into maps $a_i:U_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[t]$ whose two restrictions to each overlap agree. The covering is fpqc by [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site], so [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], with $T=U$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[t]$, gives a unique map $a:U\to X$ restricting to the $a_i$. Step 2 then gives a unique section $s$ restricting to all $s_i$. This proves existence and uniqueness of gluing on each covering family.

The gluing just proved is compatible with rings: if $s_i$ and $t_i$ glue to $s,t$, the sum $s+t$ restricts to $s_i+t_i$, the product $st$ to $s_it_i$, and $0,1$ restrict to $0,1$. Uniqueness therefore makes the inverse of the restriction-to-matching-families bijection a ring homomorphism. Equivalently, for any commutative ring $R$, glue a matching family of ring maps $R\to\mathcal O_S(U_i)$ one element at a time; the same separatedness calculation proves that the glued function preserves $+,\cdot,0,1$, and is unique. Hence the presheaf satisfies the ring-valued sheaf condition on these covering families. To verify every covering sieve, let $\mathscr R$ cover $U$ and let $(x_h)$ be a matching family on it. By [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site], choose a covering family $f_i:U_i\to U$ contained in $\mathscr R$, and glue $(x_{f_i})$ to $s$. For $h:V\to U$ in $\mathscr R$, the pullback along $h$ of the sieve generated by $(f_i)$ covers $V$ by the pullback axiom of a Grothendieck topology. Choose a covering family $g_j:V_j\to V$ contained in that pullback sieve, again using the cited description of covering sieves. Each $h\circ g_j$ factors as $f_{i(j)}\circ q_j$ for some $q_j:V_j\to U_{i(j)}$. Functoriality and the matching-family equations give $g_j^\sharp(h^\sharp(s))=q_j^\sharp(f_{i(j)}^\sharp(s))=q_j^\sharp(x_{f_{i(j)}})=x_{h\circ g_j}=g_j^\sharp(x_h)$. Separatedness from step 3 applied to $(g_j)$ gives $h^\sharp(s)=x_h$. Uniqueness follows by restricting to $(f_i)$. Thus the presheaf satisfies the sheaf condition for every covering sieve.
